raw.cause: The logger's channel is created with ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY) under the prio-inversion build. Its receive thread therefore keeps its own low priority instead of inheriting display's priority 30. The priority-20 media job keeps every CPU busy for 45 ms out of each 50 ms, so it preempts logger whenever display is SEND- or REPLY-blocked on it. Logger only gets the CPU in media's 5 ms sleep window, which turns a 2 ms busy_ms() handler into a ~47-53 ms wait. The waits land either before MsgReceive (e.g. 101852→102594: 45 ms SEND-blocked) or between MsgReceive and MsgReply (e.g. 103068→103176: 47.6 ms). Fast cycles of about 2 ms happen when the request lands in media's idle gap.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (run_logger), causing slow MsgReceive/MsgReply to display's MsgSend
raw.fix_summary: Drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so logger's receiving thread inherits display's priority 30 and outranks media (priority 20) while serving it. This is what COCKPIT_FIXED=1 already does; make it unconditional, or simply serve the logger via name_attach() like the other servers. If logging truly must never compete with real work, change the contract instead: make log_line asynchronous (MsgSendPulse or a queue drained by a separate display thread) so display never waits on logger.
